title: The World through the Computer: Computer Augmented Interaction with Real World Environments
authors: Jun Rekimoto; Katashi Nagao
takeaway: Look at a physical object through a handheld display to reveal contextual information.
bullets: Recognize a printed colour-code ID and overlay its associated information.
Use real-world situations as implicit input rather than navigating desktop menus.
limitations: Wired workstation prototype, limited 4-bit colour IDs and small display. ID recognition is not 6DoF object tracking or markerless scene understanding.
reading_depth: full-text-read: complete8page author paper including system, applications, implementation, comparison, limitations and references

title: Tangible Bits: Towards Seamless Interfaces between People, Bits and Atoms

bullets: metaDESK uses physical landmarks to control a digital geographic space.

limitations: A vision and prototype paper, not proof of a universal tangible-interface advantage.
reading_depth: complete-paper-body-read

title: Teddy: A Sketching Interface for 3D Freeform Design

limitations: Approximate rounded models, not precise CAD; original implementation produces sphere-topology surfaces.
reading_depth: full-text-read: complete body, figures/captions, evaluation, limitations and references

authors: Andrew Irlitti, Mesut Latifoglu, Thuong Hoang, Brandon Victor Syiem, Frank Vetere
takeaway: A shared-looking object is not always a shared-controllable object.

limitations: Qualitative study of 18 people in six triads; one congruent workspace and card-sorting tasks; volumetric objects can suggest control they do not provide.
